October 8, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[1 comment](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-excel-for-payroll-why-indian-smes-are-making-the-switch-in-2026/#comments)


Let’s be honest. If you run a small business in India with 10 to 50 employees, there’s a good chance your “payroll system” is a colour-coded Excel sheet that one person in your office truly understands.


And it works. Until it doesn’t.


A missed PF deposit costs you 5% to 25% in damages. One wrong TDS calculation snowballs into a ₹2 lakh penalty. A delayed Form 16 for just 30 days across 100 employees? That’s ₹3 lakh in fines under Section 272A.


Excel doesn’t warn you about any of this. It just sits there, doing exactly what you told it to, even when what you told it is wrong.


According to a 2026 report by Select Software Reviews, 51% of small businesses worldwide still use spreadsheets for payroll. In India, that number is likely higher because of the sheer volume of micro and small enterprises. But here’s the shift: India’s payroll services market has hit $1.91 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach $2.74 billion by 2031. The reason? Government mandated digital filings for EPFO, ESIC, and GST have made manual spreadsheet payroll increasingly risky.


This blog breaks down the real cost of running payroll on Excel, compares it side by side with SalaryBox, and gives you a clear framework to decide when (and whether) you should make the switch.


## The Real Problem with Excel Payroll (It’s Not What You Think)


The problem isn’t that Excel can’t do calculations. It absolutely can. The problem is that Excel has no guardrails.


There’s no system that stops you from entering the wrong PF rate. No alert when you miss a statutory deadline. No audit trail when someone edits a formula. No way for employees to check their own payslips without calling HR.


Let’s look at what actually goes wrong:


### 1. Formula Errors Are Silent and Expensive


In payroll software, the PF calculation is hardcoded: 12% of basic salary, capped at ₹15,000 per month. In Excel, it’s a formula that someone wrote months ago. If that formula references the wrong cell, or if someone accidentally drags it, the error propagates across every employee. You won’t know until EPFO rejects your ECR file or an employee files a complaint.


### 2. Compliance Is 100% on You


India has at least 8 statutory payroll deadlines every single month:


Deadline Due Date Penalty for Missing


PF deposit 15th of the month 5% to 25% damages + 12% interest


ESI deposit 15th of the month 12% annual interest


TDS deposit 7th of the month 1% per month interest


Professional Tax State specific Up to 3x unpaid amount (Karnataka)


Form 24Q (TDS return) Quarterly ₹200 per day


Form 16 15th June ₹100 per employee per day


PF ECR filing 15th of the month ₹500 per day late


ESI return Half yearly Interest + penalty


Excel gives you no reminders for any of these. One busy month and you’re looking at penalties that cost more than a year of payroll software.


### 3. The “One Person” Problem


In most small businesses, one person (usually the accountant or office manager) owns the Excel payroll file. They know the formulas, the macros, the colour codes. When that person goes on leave, falls sick, or quits, your entire payroll system walks out with them.


Payroll software eliminates this. Any authorised user can run payroll because the system holds the logic, not the person.


### 4. Employee Queries Eat Up Hours


At a company with 50+ employees, HR typically handles 10 to 20 salary related queries every month. “Why is my PF contribution different?” “Where is my payslip?” “My tax deduction seems wrong.”


With Excel, answering each query means opening the file, finding the right tab, tracing the formulas, and explaining it over the phone. With SalaryBox, employees open the app and see their own payslip, tax breakup, and PF details. Zero HR involvement.


### 5. Multi State Compliance Is Nearly Impossible


If you have employees in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, each state has different professional tax slabs, different LWF rules, and different due dates. Managing this in Excel means maintaining separate calculation sheets per state and updating them every time a state revises its rates.


Payroll software handles this automatically. SalaryBox already has built in professional tax slabs for every Indian state.

## Where Excel Still Wins (Let’s Be Fair)


Before we go further, let’s acknowledge where Excel genuinely makes sense:


**Fewer than 10 employees:** If you have a small team, salaries don’t change often, and you’re comfortable with formulas, Excel works fine. The compliance burden is manageable.


**Highly customised pay structures:** Some businesses have unusual pay components that off the shelf software doesn’t support. Excel gives you complete flexibility.


**Zero budget:** Excel comes with Microsoft Office, which most businesses already have. Payroll software has a monthly cost, even if it’s small.


**One time projects:** If you’re paying contract workers for a short project and don’t need ongoing payroll processing, Excel is simpler.


The honest answer is: if your business has fewer than 15 employees, no multi state presence, and you’re confident in your compliance knowledge, Excel will probably serve you fine for now.


But the moment you cross 15 to 20 employees, things start breaking.

## Real Penalty Scenarios: What Excel Payroll Can Cost You


Let’s look at actual penalty scenarios that happen to Indian SMEs running payroll on Excel:


### Scenario 1: Late PF Deposit


Your accountant was busy with GST filing and forgot to deposit PF by the 15th. The delay is 4 months.


- Monthly PF amount: ₹90,000 (50 employees)
- Arrears: ₹3,60,000
- Interest at 12% per annum: ₹14,400
- Damages at 15% (for 4 to 6 month delay): ₹54,000
- **Total penalty: ₹68,400**


That’s more than most companies spend on payroll software in an entire year.


### Scenario 2: Wrong TDS Calculation


A formula error in your Excel sheet calculated TDS at 10% instead of 20% for employees in the higher slab. The mistake ran for 6 months before anyone noticed.


- TDS shortfall: ₹1,20,000
- Interest at 1% per month for 6 months: ₹7,200
- Potential penalty under Section 271C: up to ₹1,20,000
- **Total exposure: up to ₹2,47,200**


### Scenario 3: Form 16 Delayed


Your one person payroll team quit in May. The new person couldn’t figure out the Excel file in time. Form 16 was issued 20 days late for 50 employees.


- Penalty: ₹100 per employee per day × 50 × 20 = ₹1,00,000


**None of these scenarios are hypothetical.** They happen to real Indian businesses every year because Excel has no safety net.

## When Should You Switch from Excel to Payroll Software?


Here’s a simple checklist. If you tick 3 or more, it’s time to switch:


- You have more than 15 employees
- Your payroll takes more than one full working day each month
- You’ve received even one compliance notice or penalty
- You have employees in more than one state
- Generating Form 16 takes more than 30 minutes
- Employees regularly ask about their salary breakup or payslip
- Only one person in your company can run payroll
- You manually calculate PF, ESI, or TDS using formulas
- Your Excel file has more than 8 tabs
- You’ve ever had an EPFO ECR rejection due to data errors


**Ticked 3 or more? You’re spending more on Excel payroll than you realise.**

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Excel really free for payroll?


On paper, yes. In practice, no. The hidden costs of HR time, error correction, compliance penalties, and manual payslip generation add up to ₹1.2 to ₹1.4 lakh per year for a 50 person company. That’s before counting even one compliance penalty, which can range from ₹15,000 to ₹3 lakh depending on the violation.


### At what company size should I switch from Excel to payroll software?


The sweet spot is around 15 to 20 employees. Below 10, Excel is manageable. Above 15, the compliance burden, employee queries, and processing time start outweighing the “zero cost” advantage of Excel. If you have employees in multiple states, switch even earlier.


### How long does it take to migrate from Excel to SalaryBox?


Most businesses complete the migration in 2 weeks. Week one covers data import and setup. Week two is a parallel payroll run to verify everything matches. SalaryBox’s onboarding team assists throughout the process.


### Will I lose my old payroll data?


No. You keep your Excel files as archives. SalaryBox can import historical employee data, and your old files remain available for reference. We recommend keeping Excel archives for at least 7 years for audit compliance.


### Can SalaryBox handle my specific salary structure?


Yes. SalaryBox supports custom salary components, including HRA, DA, special allowances, LTA, meal coupons, and performance bonuses. You can configure monthly, daily, or hourly pay cycles with 26 day, 30 day, or calendar month calculations.


### What if I have employees in different states?


SalaryBox has built in professional tax slabs for every Indian state and automatically applies the correct rate based on each employee’s work location. It also handles Labour Welfare Fund (LWF) deductions where applicable.


### Is my payroll data safe on cloud software?


SalaryBox uses encrypted cloud storage with role based access control. Unlike an Excel file sitting on someone’s laptop (which can be copied, emailed, or lost), cloud payroll data is protected, backed up daily, and accessible only to authorised users.


### Does SalaryBox work for companies with fewer than 10 employees?


Absolutely. While Excel might work for very small teams, SalaryBox’s affordable pricing means even a 5 person company can benefit from automated PF/ESI calculations, digital payslips, and compliance reminders. The question isn’t company size but whether you value your time and want to avoid compliance risks.
